supermarket.note: Ask the butcher to cut the ribs into 2 to 3 inch pieces when you buy them.

tools.name: Mortar and pestle
tools.note: A zip-top bag and a rolling pin can stand in for cracking the peppercorns.

tools.name: Cheesecloth
tools.note: Kitchen string ties it closed, and a large tea infuser can be used instead.

tools.name: Colander
tools.note: A large sieve or a clean kitchen towel can be used to drain food instead.

tools.name: Stockpot
tools.note: Use a large one, since it holds the soup while it simmers.

tools.name: Dipping Bowl
tools.note: Four small bowls are listed, and any small dishes can stand in.

steps.title: Prep ribs, garlic and dipping bowls
points: Rinse the ribs under cold water.
Rub off the loose papery outer skin from the garlic heads but leave them whole and unpeeled.
Slice the chillies into thin rings, divide them among the dipping bowls, and pour 1 tablespoon of the dipping soy sauce into each bowl.

steps.title: Toast and crack peppercorns
points: Put the peppercorns in the small frying pan over medium-low heat.
Toast them for 2 to 3 minutes, shaking the pan, until fragrant.
Tip them onto a plate to cool, then crack them coarsely in the mortar.
Tie them in the cheesecloth or put them in the infuser.

steps.title: Blanch ribs
points: Fill the large pot about two-thirds full of water and bring it to a boil over high heat.
Add the ribs and boil for 5 minutes, until grey foam rises to the surface.
Drain the ribs in the colander and rinse each piece under warm running water to wash off the foam.

steps.title: Simmer the ribs
points: Put the 10 cups of water, the blanched ribs, the garlic heads, and the pepper bag in the clean stockpot.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then turn the heat down to low so the soup barely bubbles.
Partly cover the pot and simmer for 1 1/2 hours, skimming off any foam or fat every 20 minutes, until the meat is tender and pulls away from the bone.

steps.title: Season the broth
points: Stir in the 1 tablespoon light soy sauce, the dark soy sauce, the sugar, and the salt.
Simmer for 10 more minutes.
Taste the broth and add more salt if it needs it.
Lift out the pepper bag and discard it.

steps.title: Serve the ribs
points: Ladle the ribs and broth into bowls, adding a few garlic cloves to each.
Serve with rice and the chilli soy sauce for dipping the meat.
The soft garlic can be squeezed out of its skin and eaten with the rice.

troubleshooting.problem: The broth is cloudy and has a scummy taste
troubleshooting.solution: The ribs were not blanched and rinsed, or the soup boiled hard. Always blanch the ribs in the separate pot and keep the stockpot at a gentle simmer.

troubleshooting.problem: The soup is not peppery enough
troubleshooting.solution: Crack the peppercorns well after toasting, and leave the bag in for the full simmer.

troubleshooting.problem: The meat is still tough after 1 1/2 hours
troubleshooting.solution: Ribs vary in thickness. Keep simmering and check every 15 minutes until a rib pulls apart easily.
Too much water evaporated. Add hot water a little at a time until it tastes right, then bring it back to a simmer.
